description: DJ EARth reimagines how we interact with space data by translating Earth Information Center visual frames into live audio signals. Driven by signal processing and intuitive software design, our team turns static satellite monitoring into a voice you can hear/making planetary insights accessible to everyone worldwide.
summary: DJ_EARth is an interactive web-based sonification studio that transforms NASA Earth observation imagery into music. Designed as an eight-track "Earth Sessions" album, the platform maps planetary datasets including Earth temperature, night lights, air quality (NO₂), storms, ocean currents, wind speed, hurricanes, and altitude to distinct musical instruments such as harmonica, piano, flute, electric guitar, harp, drums, violin, and bass. Users click or use keyboard sliders to sample map pixels, hear color-coded scientific values translated into musical scales, upload their own images, or ask the "Hey DJ" voice assistant to play a country's temperature profile. By turning complex satellite visualizations into intuitive auditory experiences, DJ_EARth makes climate and atmospheric science accessible to curious learners, students, and blind or low-vision audiences without requiring prior technical or musical expertise.
details:
What It Does & How It Works DJ_EARth turns satellite and Earth-science maps into an interactive musical studio. Users select from eight planetary tracks Night Lights (Piano), Earth Temperature (Harmonica), Air Quality (Flute), Storms (Electric Guitar), Ocean Currents (Harp), Wind Speed (Drums), Hurricane (Violin), and Altitude (Bass) and sample data points across reference maps or their own uploaded PNG/JPEG images. An HTML5 Canvas engine reads pixel RGB values and maps color legends (such as NASA Goddard's 0–6 thermal scale mapped across Do–Si) or unsupervised 1D k-means clusters ("Learn from image" mode) into musical pitches. The Air Quality track also features an NO₂ Lab prototype using a supervised five-nearest-labeled-color model trained on NASA Aura OMI maps (March 2015–2019 vs. March 2020), while the "Hey DJ" voice assistant uses browser speech recognition to play six-point landmass temperature melodies for any requested country.

Benefits & Intended Impact Satellite maps often require scientific training to interpret and remain inaccessible to blind or low-vision users. DJ_EARth lowers that barrier by translating spatial environmental data into immediate, intuitive soundscapes helping blind people, students, educators, and curious listeners hear planetary patterns, compare regional differences, and engage emotionally with Earth science.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software

  • Frontend & Audio: HTML5, CSS3, and modular vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), using the HTML5 Canvas API for pixel color sampling, the Web Audio API for real-time synthesis and live waveform visualization, and the Web Speech API for voice interaction.
  • Audio Samples & Data Prep: Open-source FluidR3 instrument samples (harmonica, electric guitar, harp, and violin) paired with custom Web Audio synthesizers, plus Python for reference asset preparation.
  • Collaboration & Hosting: Git, GitHub, Visual Studio Code, and GitHub Pages.

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

  • Creative Concept: Framed as a tactile vinyl turntable and recording studio ("The Earth Sessions"), pairing each planetary force with an expressive instrument voice.
  • Scientific Integrity: Loudness (volume) is strictly decoupled from data pitch so volume adjustments never distort scientific readings; unreadable or dark map pixels are rejected rather than falsely reported as zero; and clear labels distinguish historical reference datasets from real-time weather.
  • Accessibility & Privacy: Every interactive map supports full keyboard slider navigation and screen-reader ARIA live announcements, and all user-uploaded images are processed locally in the browser without leaving the user's device.
